rationale: Validation status is fail with two dead_checks/uncovered_requirements: FR4 and SR1. Examining the actual mutants: the SR1 mutant (constant_change) changes the reported missing tap from x^6 to x^5 while keeping all the surrounding correct-sounding language and structure -- this is a genuine corruption of the tap identification that SR1 is supposed to catch, yet the check passed it, meaning the SR1 regex/matching logic is too permissive (matches on generic feedback-defect phrasing rather than verifying the specific claimed missing tap is x^6). The FR4 mutant (operator_swap) changes the reported period from ~28 to 255 (contradicting simulation-confirmed ground truth), which is a real, observable corruption that FR4's numeric-period extraction should have caught but did not, meaning FR4 is not cross-checking the extracted period value against the simulated ground truth (or is only checking for presence of *a* number, not its correctness at the FR4 stage while relying entirely on SR3 for correctness). Both mutants genuinely reintroduce defects relevant to their target requirements, so this is an evaluation_framework issue, not a defective-mutant issue. Per rules, mutation_score 0.75 >= 0.5 and analyzer status is warning, but validation_status is fail and the dead_check/uncovered_requirement issues take precedence, requiring revision before retention.
revision_instructions: Two requirement checks in evaluate.py are dead/uncovered per mutation analysis; both corresponding mutants genuinely reintroduce the defect they target, so the checks themselves must be strengthened (do not blame the mutants). (1) SR1: a mutant that claims the missing tap is a different bit position than the true missing tap (while retaining otherwise-correct-sounding feedback-defect prose) was not detected as failing. Rewrite the SR1 check so it extracts the specific tap/bit identification claimed by the submission and verifies it names the correct omitted tap corresponding to the actual feedback expression in the RTL (grade by comparing the claimed omitted term against the real omitted term derivable from the interface-pinned polynomial and the RTL feedback logic, not by loosely matching any of several accepted phrasings). A submission naming the wrong omitted tap must FAIL SR1 even if it uses otherwise-plausible defect vocabulary. Simplify away the ambiguous 0-indexed/1-indexed commentary noted by the analyzer and pick one consistent indexing convention for grading, applied uniformly. (2) FR4: a mutant that reports the numeric period as 255 (the full maximal-length value) instead of the true short-cycle value was not detected as failing by FR4. FR4 currently appears to only check that some integer period value is present; it must also verify that the reported period is consistent with the actual simulated behavior (cross-check the extracted numeric period against the value obtained by running the provided simulation harness on the RTL, independent of SR3). Tighten FR4 so a submission stating an incorrect period distant from the simulated ground truth fails FR4, not only SR3. Add or adjust mutants as needed to confirm both checks now discriminate correctly after the fix.
